body: Bonus-adjusted (2:1 bonuses in 2022 and 2025) price ₹46 (Mar 2020) → ATH ₹4,194 (May 2026) ≈91x; P/E 14 → 69 (4.9x) × implied EPS ~18.6x. ₹3,765 on 19 Nov 2026 (−10%). Motilal Oswal's 2020–25 study named BSE the fastest wealth creator. Drawdowns: −73% (2017–20, before), −55% (Mar 2022–Mar 2023), −35% (Jan–Mar 2025). Revenue FY23 ₹925 cr → FY26 ₹5,124 cr; OPM 34% → 68%; ROCE 12% → 60%. Early signal: in May 2023 BSE relaunched Sensex/Bankex derivatives (contract-design details unverified). Exchange-published daily options premium share was the alt-data: 11.4% (Oct 2024) → 24.4% (Sep 2025) → 26.8% (Q3 FY26). The SEBI Nov 2024 rule allowing one weekly index expiry per exchange made BSE's Sensex expiry a scarce slot. A near-zero marginal cost platform meant each volume gain flowed to profit. In Mar 2023 the stock was at P/E ~29 with EPS about to grow 12x. Risks: regulatory single point of failure (expiry-day changes, talk of monthly-only expiries, STT); its customers are mostly losing retail F&O traders (see insight:sebi-fo-losses). Lesson: exchange operating leverage plus a free, daily market-share series let an alert investor size the earnings inflection early.

data.early_signals: 2023 derivatives relaunch; daily premium-share data; SEBI 2024 expiry rule
data.note: Prices: screener.in weekly closes, split/bonus-adjusted. P/E = trailing (TTM); implied EPS x = price multiple / P/E multiple.

title: BSE Ltd 2020–2026: options-expiry market share + operating leverage, ~91x
